kicker: Ember · Science · Test on Wed 18 Nov
title: Force and hydraulics equations
sub: Every equation for the forces test on one page, then use each one. About 15 minutes. Print the paper and test yourself from memory the night before.
skill: Equation first: write the equation in words, then the numbers, then the answer with its unit.
target: Before any calculation, write the equation. If you know the force and the area, ask: am I finding pressure (÷) or force (×)?

sections.sub: Read it, then cover it and say each one out loud.

blocks.html:
Weight
weight = mass × gravitational field strength  (W = m × g)
N = kg × N/kg. On Earth g = 9.8 N/kg (some questions round it to 10: use the number they give).
Resultant force
same direction: add; opposite directions: bigger − smaller
N, pointing the way of the bigger force.
Hooke’s Law (springs)
force = spring constant × extension  (F = k × e)
N = N/m × m. Extension = new length − original length. In words: double the force, double the extension.
Moment (turning)
moment = force × distance  (M = F × d)
N m. d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot (cm gives N cm). Balanced: total clockwise moment = total anticlockwise moment.
Pressure
pressure = force ÷ area  (P = F ÷ A)
N/m² = Pa (pascal); area in cm² gives N/cm². Turned round: force = pressure × area, area = force ÷ pressure.
Hydraulics
1. pressure = force ÷ area (small piston)
2. force = pressure × area (big piston)  (F₁ ÷ A₁ = F₂ ÷ A₂)
The pressure is the same at both pistons. Keep both areas in the same unit.

Why hydraulics works. A liquid cannot be squashed (compressed). So pushing on it at one end raises the pressure everywhere in the liquid, by the same amount. The big piston has a bigger area, so the same pressure makes a bigger force. The catch: the small piston has to move much further than the big one.

blocks.h: Cover the table. Can you say…
items: the unit of each: N, N/kg, N/m, N m, N/m² (Pa)

blocks.q: Which is the equation for weight?
blocks.why: W = m × g. A 1 kg mass on Earth weighs 9.8 N.

blocks.q: Which is the equation for pressure?
blocks.why: Pressure is force per area, so force ÷ area. In the mock you multiplied: this is the one to fix.

blocks.q: What is the unit of a moment?
blocks.why: Moment = force × distance, so N × m = N m. N/m is the spring constant; N/m² is pressure.

blocks.q: What is the unit of gravitational field strength?
blocks.why: g tells you how many newtons of weight each kilogram has: 9.8 N/kg on Earth.

blocks.q: In a hydraulic jack, what is the same at the small piston and the big piston?
blocks.why: The liquid passes the pressure on equally. The big piston has more area, so it gets a bigger force.

sections.sub: Write the equation on paper first, then the numbers.

blocks.q: A dog has a mass of 20 kg. Gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg. Calculate its weight.

traps.msg: That is the mass. Weight is in newtons: multiply by 9.8.

blocks.q: A spring has a spring constant of 40 N/m. It is stretched by 0.05 m. Calculate the force.

traps.msg: You divided. Force = spring constant × extension.

blocks.q: You push a door handle with a force of 30 N. The handle is 80 cm from the hinge. Calculate the moment in N m.

traps.msg: The cm trap: change 80 cm to 0.8 m first.

blocks.q: A box weighing 600 N rests on an area of 0.2 m². Calculate the pressure on the floor.
Water pushes on a dam with a pressure of 5000 N/m². A gate in the dam has an area of 2 m². Calculate the force on the gate.
blocks.why: You want the force, so force = pressure × area = 5000 × 2 = 10 000 N.

traps.msg: You divided. To find a force from a pressure, multiply: force = pressure × area.

blocks.q: In a hydraulic jack, you push the small piston down with a force of 50 N. The small piston has an area of 2 cm². The big piston, under the car, has an area of 100 cm². Calculate the force on the big piston.

steps.p: Pressure in the liquid = force ÷ area at the small piston. What is it?
The pressure is the same at the big piston. Force = pressure × area. What is the force on the big piston?

traps.msg: You divided. Now you want a force, so multiply: force = pressure × area.

steps.p: How many times bigger is the force on the big piston than your push?

blocks.why: Pressure = 50 ÷ 2 = 25 N/cm². Force = 25 × 100 = 2500 N. The area is 50 times bigger, so the force is 50 times bigger.

blocks.q: To lift the car 1 cm, which piston moves further?
blocks.why: The liquid pushed out of the thin cylinder has to fill a wide one, so the small piston moves about 50 cm for every 1 cm the big one rises. You get a bigger force, but you push further.

blocks.q: Explain how a hydraulic jack lets a small force lift a heavy car.
starters: The small force on the small piston…
The liquid cannot be compressed, so…
The big piston has a bigger area, so…

points.t: a small force on a small area makes a pressure in the liquid
the liquid cannot be compressed, so the pressure is passed on equally to the big piston
the big piston has a bigger area, so the force on it is bigger (force = pressure × area)

mark.note: Point to the words for each tick. Did your chain end with the bigger force on the car?

paper.title: Force and hydraulics equations: from memory
paper.sub: Ember · Science · night before the test · about 10 minutes
paper.intro: Fill in the table from memory. Then do the three calculations: equation first, then numbers, then the answer with its unit. Mark it with the key at the end.

blocks.h: 1. Write each equation and its units

blocks.q: 2. A suitcase has a mass of 15 kg. Gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg. Calculate its weight.
3. A woman weighing 600 N stands on snowshoes with a total area of 0.3 m². Calculate the pressure on the snow.
4. In a hydraulic press, a force of 20 N pushes on a piston of area 4 cm². The big piston has an area of 200 cm². Calculate the force on the big piston.

selfcheck: I wrote the equation before the numbers every time.
Hydraulics: I found the pressure first, then multiplied by the big area.

marking.html:
1. weight = mass × gravitational field strength (N, kg, N/kg) · force = spring constant × extension (N, N/m, m) · moment = force × distance (N m) · pressure = force ÷ area (N/m² or Pa; N/cm²) · force = pressure × area (N) · hydraulics: pressure = force ÷ small area, then force = pressure × big area.
2. 15 × 9.8 (1) = 147 N (1)
3. 600 ÷ 0.3 (1) = 2000 N/m² (1)
4. pressure = 20 ÷ 4 = 5 N/cm² (1); force = 5 × 200 (1) = 1000 N (1)
